items.summary: देशभर में कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी (सीजेपी) के ‘स्कूल ठीक करो’ अभियान के बाद सरकारी स्कूलों के हालात पर चर्चा होने लगी है. इस बीच गुजरात में एक ही सरकारी स्कूल के लिए एएनआई और न्यूज़ 18 गुजराती ने वीडियो बनाया है. दोनों ने वीडियो में बताया कि स्कूल इतने अच्छे हैं कि एडमिशन के लिए लाइन लगी हुई हैं. हालांकि, दोनों ने यह बताने की जहमत नहीं उठाई कि इसी प्रदेश में बाकी स्कूलों के हालात क्या हैं. गौरतलब है कि गुजरात में ड्रापआउट रेट ‘रेड जोन’ में हैं. प्रदेश में दो साल में 75 प्राइमरी स्कूल बंद हो चुके हैं. 9442 क्लासरूम की कमी है और 2674 स्कूल शिफ्ट में चल रहे हैं. इतना ही नहीं गुजरात में हर 29 छात्र पर एक शिक्षक हैं जबकि राष्ट्रीय औसत 24 छात्रों का है. गुजरात के 2335 स्कूल सिर्फ एक शिक्षक के भरोसे चल रहे हैं, जिनमें कुल 80 हजार छात्र पढ़ रहे हैं. स्कूलों को ठीक करने की जिम्मेदारी सरकार की हैं और उनकी कमियों को उजागर कर सरकार के संज्ञान में लाने की जिम्मेदारी मीडिया की लेकिन इतनी कमियां होने के बावजूद एक ही स्कूल के कसीदे पढ़े जा रहे. देखिए यह सारांश. एनएल सारांश: राम मंदिर पर शंकराचार्यों और कांग्रेस का इनकार कितना सही, कितना गलत 1950 का एक्ट: सुप्रीम कोर्ट के डीसी को ताकत देने और सीएम हेमंता के दावे का सारांश

items.title: One school, zero scrutiny: How ANI, News18 sold Gujarat’s school ‘model’
items.summary: As the Cockroach Janta Party’s ‘School Thik Karo’ campaign draws national attention to the state of government schools, ANI and News18 Gujarati have gone the other way – holding up a single school in Gujarat’s Botad district as evidence that the state’s public education system is flourishing. Both outlets built their stories around PM SHRI Dr Sarvapalli Radhakrishnan Nagar Primary School No. 24, citing long waiting lists and parents choosing it over private options. News18 ’s headline claimed the school “puts private schools to shame”. ANI ’s three-minute video carried interviews with the principal, students and parents, framing it much the same way: 250 children on a waiting list, government schools becoming parents’ “top choice”. Neither outlet disclosed whether the coverage was paid promotion, and neither offered the wider picture. Moreover, government data tells a starkly different story. According to the Ministry of Education’s UDISE+ report , only 54.5 percent of Gujarat’s 1.15 crore government-school students complete their education through Class 12. The state has one teacher for every 29 students, compared with a national average of 24, and 2,335 schools run with a single teacher for over 8,000 children between them. A parliamentary reply shows Gujarat recorded the country’s highest number of out-of-school children in 2025-26 – 2.4 lakh children, including 1.1 lakh girls, a 341 percent jump over the previous year. The state assembly was also told of a shortfall of 9,442 classrooms, forcing 2,674 schools to run in shifts. This isn’t the first time either outlet has done this: ANI and PTI ran similarly uncritical coverage of Gujarat’s PM SHRI schools back in June and July. Watch this explainer for more. A quarter-century of Modi governance calls for questions and a hamper. To mark the occasion, we have offers for subscribers and other readers .

items.title: Gujarat High Court rejects Asaram's plea for 20-day temporary bail to meet ailing wife
items.summary: The Gujarat High Court on Wednesday rejected a plea by self-styled godman Asaram seeking 20 days' temporary bail to meet his wife, who is undergoing treatment at a hospital in Ahmedabad [Ashumal @ Asharam v State of Gujarat] . A Division Bench of Justices Gita Gopi and LS Pirzada declined the plea after considering a medical report stating that Asaram's wife had responded well to treatment and was expected to be discharged within 2-3 days. “When the patient has responded well to the treatment and both the doctors have opined that she would be discharged within the next two to three days, we do not find any reason to allow the application of the petitioner, who is presently in Jodhpur Jail, Rajasthan,” said the Court. However, the Court allowed Asaram to seek permission from the jail authorities to communicate with his wife through video conferencing. Justice Gita Gopi and Justice LS Pirzada Asaram was sentenced to life imprisonment by a Gandhinagar court in a rape case. The court convicted Asaram in a case registered in 2013 for raping a woman disciple from Surat repeatedly between 2001 and 2006. The girl was living at his ashram in Motera. Asaram is also serving a life sentence in another case of raping a minor girl in Rajasthan in 2013. The present plea was filed on the ground that Asaram's wife, who is 83 years old, was critically ill and had been admitted to a hospital in Naroda. The Court had on September 29 directed the local police to verify the claim regarding her illness. During today's hearing, Advocate Ashish Dagli, appearing for Asaram, told the Court that his wife was critically ill. Seeking temporary bail, Dagli submitted that Asaram was 87 and had complied with the terms and conditions imposed during his previous temporary release. Dagli also submitted that Asaram was in Rajasthan and would remain there after the period of temporary release. He added that he was willing to bear the expenses of the proposed visit. The Court also noted the police report that Asaram's wife was being looked after by her relatives and disciples and that a personal doctor was present at the hospital along with the two treating doctors. Taking note of the submissions, the Court declined to grant Asaram temporary bail. This is not the first time Asaram has sought temporary release from custody. items.title: Karnataka High Court permits man to donate kidney altruistically to unrelated recipient; State to frame guidelines
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Wednesday permitted a 52-year-old bachelor to donate one of his kidneys altruistically to a deserving, unrelated recipient. Justice Suraj Govindaraj passed the order after taking note of a medical report submitted by the Institute of Nephro Urology at Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru. Pertinently, the State government informed the Court that it is framing guidelines laying down a mechanism for dealing with cases of altruistic organ donation. Justice Suraj Govindraj The petitioner had approached the High Court seeking permission to donate one of his kidneys to a deserving recipient without seeking any monetary consideration or other benefit. The petitioner told the Court that he is a bachelor who has been living independently for more than 16 years. His mother and brother are his close family members, but neither is dependent on him. The petitioner expressed his willingness to donate one of his kidneys to any deserving recipient, irrespective of caste, religion, financial status or personal relationship, while maintaining confidentiality regarding the identities of the donor and recipient. The petitioner initially approached a hospital during 2015-16, when a compatible recipient was identified on June 4, 2016. However, the proposed donation could not proceed after his brother objected to the donation. Subsequently, after his mother and brother consented to his decision to make an altruistic donation, the petitioner approached the High Court seeking appropriate directions. The issue first came up before the Court on August 25, when the Bench noted that it was the second case involving a person seeking to donate an organ altruistically to an unrelated third party. The Court had also taken note of the submission made by petitioner's counsel SV Joga Rao that several other persons could be willing to come forward to make altruistic organ donations. In view of the possibility of similar cases arising in the future, the Court called upon the State to ascertain whether any mechanism or policy was already available for dealing with altruistic organ donations involving donors and recipients who had no familial or other recognised relationship. The Bench had further observed that in the absence of a defined procedure, a willing donor may be required to approach the High Court for directions before the proposed donation could be considered by the competent authorities. The Court also highlighted the time-sensitive nature of organ transplantation

items.title: DHCBA seeks withdrawal of UP Police FIR against lawyer over X post on Ayush Malik case in Allahabad HC
items.summary: The Delhi High Court Bar Association (DHCBA) has asked the Uttar Pradesh Director General of Police to withdraw or close a first information report (FIR) registered by Shamli police against Delhi-based advocate Syed Kaif Hasan, over his X post about a case recently decided by the Allahabad High Court. Hasan had reportedly written that the Allahabad High Court reprimanded the Uttar Pradesh Police over Shamli youth Ayush Malik's illegal confinement at his home . Malik had been illegally detained by his family following his conversion from Hinduism to Islam. The police denied the claim that it was reprimanded by High Court and registered an FIR against Hasan and others. In a letter to DGP Rajeev Krishna, the DHCBA on September 29 said that Hasan's post was "expressly presented as an update of the proceedings and that the written order was, at that stage, awaited." The association said it "does not seek to pre-empt any lawful investigation" but warned that such action may have a chilling effect on the legitimate reporting of judicial proceedings. The letter followed a September 21 resolution in which the DHCBA condemned the "highhanded and uncalled-for action" of the UP police against Hasan, its member. Shamil Police have registered an FIR under Section 353(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) against Hasan and five others. The FIR, in Hindi, rejects the claim that the court had reprimanded the Shamli Police. It states that the court had not sought a counter-affidavit from the police, and described the matter as a dispute between a father and son. Shamli Police's cyber cell in a recent communication to X Corp described @kaifsyedhasan as a "fake Twitter account" created by "an unknown person." The notice invoked Section 66D of the Information Technology Act, which deals with cheating by personation. It sought the account's IP address, linked email and mobile number, and device details. In a response posted on X, Hasan told the police that his account was based of the High Court's oral observations, which were not recorded in the order passed subsequently. "I am advocate in the same court. You may take action in accordance with law against those who are really distorting anything. But don't intimidate me please. Oral observations are different and heard by those present in court," Hasan said.

items.title: Is the master of roster mastering the roster?
items.summary: The Chief Justice is the master of the roster. But when control of the roster determines which judge hears which sensitive case, the question is no longer merely administrative. It is about who decides which cases are heard and by whom - and whether the established norms of roster allocation are being followed. The Medha Roopam listing: Where did the roster go? The controversy begins with a case that should have been routine: a challenge by Gautam Buddha Nagar District Magistrate Medha Roopam to the Allahabad High Court judgment quashing the National Security Act detention of Delhi University student Akriti Chaudhary. The Supreme Court matter was heard on September 23 by Justices Satish Chandra Sharma and N Kotiswar Singh . The difficulty is that the published roster did not ordinarily assign habeas corpus and preventive detention matters to Justice Sharma’s Bench. That category was assigned to a Bench headed by Justice BV Nagarathna . A special assignment is not, by itself, unlawful. But that is precisely why the question cannot be brushed aside: who authorised the departure from the ordinary roster and where is that departure recorded? If the roster is published as the Court’s mechanism for transparent allocation, an exception to the roster cannot be allowed to become an administrative secret. The matter became more sensitive because Roopam is the daughter of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The Allahabad High Court had not merely quashed the detention; it had imposed strictures and directed recovery of ₹5 lakh from the salaries of officials. On September 23, the Supreme Court’s initial order stated that the “operation of the impugned judgment” would remain stayed, “particularly” paragraphs 27 to 33. The wording created an immediate ambiguity over whether the student’s detention had also been revived. When an order affecting personal liberty requires correction within 24 hours, the question is not merely what the Court ultimately meant, but why the first order was framed with such ambiguity in the first place. There was another unusual feature. During the hearing, after briefly hearing the Solicitor General and senior counsel for the State, the Bench muted the audio of the virtual proceedings and closed media access to the video feed for the remainder of the hearing. No reason for restricting access was publicly stated. In a case already raising questions about listing and roster allocation, the sudden loss of public access to the hearing adds

items.title: Delhi High Court seeks Centre's reply on PIL against Aadhaar authentication for domestic LPG cylinders
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Wednesday sought responses from the Central government and oil and gas companies on a plea challenging the mandate that by October 1, domestic LPG consumers must complete biometric Aadhaar authentication (BAA) to book refills at the regulated price [Pulkit Luthra v. Union of India & Ors] . A Division Bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia said that it will consider the case on Monday (October 5). The Court remarked, "Everybody doesn’t have Aadhaar in this country, but they too are consuming LPG." Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia Delhi High Court Everybody doesn’t have Aadhaar in this country, but they too are consuming LPG. The Court passed the order while dealing with a public interest litigation (PIL) filed by Pulkit Luthra, a practising advocate who is 75% visually disabled. Luthra has challenged the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas' September 17 letter to oil marketing companies and its September 19 press release announcing the mandatory biometric authentication requirement. He has argued that the requirement, particularly iris authentication involving blinking of the eyes, creates serious difficulties for persons with visual disabilities. According to Luthra, consumers "unwilling or unable" to authenticate would instead be permitted to obtain LPG at market prices in 5kg or 10kg cylinders, subject to availability. He contends that this is not an adequate alternative as consumers would lose access not only to the regulated/subsidised price, but potentially also to the regular 14.2 kg domestic cylinder. Further, he states that the requirement of Aadhaar authentication travels beyond the permissible scope of Section 7 of the Aadhaar Act, 2016 and fails the test of the Supreme Court's judgment in KS Puttaswamy . "Consequently, compulsory Aadhaar authentication, being an intrusion upon the fundamental right to privacy, must be authorised by law. The impugned directions, falling outside Section 7 of the Aadhaar Act, 2016 and unsupported by any other enabling statutory provision, cannot impose such a requirement by mere executive fiat. They consequently fail the requirement of legality recognised in KS Puttaswamy," the plea states. He has also argued that the new framework is arbitrary, disproportionate and violates Articles 14 and 21 of the Constitution and the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016. items.title: How can we make International Arbitration truly successful in India?
items.summary: Recently, I had the opportunity to interact with a very seasoned and experienced Senior Counsel from Singapore. Our conversation moved towards a subject that has been discussed extensively in India over the last few years: can India become a global hub for international arbitration? His answer surprised me. He said, quite simply, that India can never become an international arbitration hub. At first, I thought this was criticism. It wasn't. His reasoning was far more interesting. According to him, India is too large an economy, too significant a market and too important a participant in global commerce to merely aspire to become an "arbitration hub" in the conventional sense of the term. Countries such as Singapore, London, Paris or Hong Kong have developed themselves as preferred seats for international arbitration for a variety of historical, commercial, institutional and legal reasons. India, however, has an opportunity to build something much larger. India does not necessarily need to become an international arbitration hub. India has the potential to become one of the countries that could shape the future of international arbitration. That, in my view, is a far more ambitious and meaningful objective. India's position in the global economy is changing rapidly. India is attracting international capital, global businesses are expanding their operations here, Indian companies are investing overseas, supply chains are becoming increasingly integrated and cross-border commercial relationships are becoming more complex. With greater commerce comes an inevitable consequence: more disputes. The question, therefore, is not whether India will have international commercial disputes. We will. The real question is where businesses will choose to resolve those disputes, and whether they will have confidence in choosing India. An international investor does not merely evaluate the tax regime, infrastructure, market size or availability of skilled manpower before entering a country. Increasingly, sophisticated investors also look at something less visible but equally important. What happens when the relationship breaks down? Can I enforce my contract? items.title: Right to be forgotten: Delhi High Court says Meta exempt from directive to de-index judgments
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Wednesday clarified that certain directions contained in a May 29 single-judge Bench ruling on the 'right to be forgotten' do not apply to Meta platforms such as Facebook [ Meta Platforms vs Mr X & Ors ]. A Division Bench of Justice C Hari Shankar and Justice Nivedita Anil Sharma issued the clarification, while dealing with a plea moved by Meta in the matter. By a May 29 ruling, a single-judge Bench of the Court had directed search-engine operators, including Google, to de-index certain judicial records from name-based search results. In this regard, the May 29 judgment had said, “The concerned respondents/ search engine operators/ legal data base platforms are directed to de-index, and disable, across all platforms and domains, name-based search functionality in respect of the judgments/orders/news articles complained of in the petition.” It had also directed law database, Indian Kanoon to restrict name-based searches for these records, although the platform was allowed to continue giving users access to these records through other parameters such as case number, citation, court and date. Indian Kanoon has filed an appeal against this ruling, which is yet to be decided by a Division Bench of the Court. Meta, meanwhile, moved a plea questioning the applicability of the May 29 ruling to its platform Facebook, particularly the directions to de-index judgments and disable name-based searches to certain judicial records. Representing Meta, Senior Advocate Mukul Rohatgi explained that since Facebook is not a search engine, it cannot comply with such de-indexing directions. "I have no grievance with the judgment. I have taken down the URLs. I am Facebook, I am not a search engine ... The judgment is overbroad. I only want a clarification that having removed the complained URLs, nothing applies to me and this matter can be disposed of," he said. Senior Advocate Mukul Rohatgi “Nobody accesses you Facebook) now; you are outdated. You (Rohatgi) will never be outdated but Facebook is outdated," Justice Shankar said in a lighter vein. The Court, however, acknowledged that the earlier directions for de-indexing certain search results to judicial records are irrelevant for Meta/ Facebook. It also recorded that the opposing parties did not object to such a clarification being made. It, therefore, closed Meta's plea after recording that the May 29 de-indexing directives do not apply to Facebook/ Meta. Senior Advocate Vivek Reddy also represented Me

items.title: HPNLU student hospitalised after suicide attempt
items.summary: A 3rd-year student of Himachal Pradesh National Law University (HPNLU), Shimla is undergoing treatment after a suicide attempt on Tuesday. The student was first taken to the Community Medical Centre at Dhami before being shifted to Indira Gandhi Medical College and Hospital, Shimla. The incident follows a ragging complaint against the student by some batchmates. In a video recorded by the student before the attempt, he alleged that the complaint is false and that the University was unwilling to properly examine the evidence despite repeated requests. He expressed frustration at having to repeatedly visit the police station and added that it had caused him considerable distress. People close to the student allege that he was under immense mental pressure after the complaint and was repeatedly harassed by the complainants, affecting his well being. They also said that the student following the ragging complaint, the student was moved to a hostel that isolated him from most of his batchmates. In a statement, HPNLU acknowledged the complaint against the student and said the matter was under consideration by the competent authorities under its Anti-Ragging Regulations. The inquiry is underway and no final findings have been reached. The statement added that the complainant had separately lodged a first information report (FIR) at Arki Police Station and that HPNLU, in compliance with its obligations under the Anti-Ragging framework had also informed Dhami Police Chowki of the matter. The university has said that presenting allegations as established facts while the inquiry is pending was premature and could prejudice the proceedings. As such, it appealed to all concerned from spreading unverified information. If you or anyone else you know are facing mental health issues or having suicidal or self-harming thoughts, please access the helpline number given below: iCall - 9152987821 (Health Helpline - Mon—Sat, 10 AM—8 PM. Languages: English, Hindi, Marathi, Gujarati, Bengali, Assamese, Kashmiri.) items.title: Bombay High Court rejects election petition against BJP MP Narayan Rane
items.summary: The Kolhapur bench of the Bombay High Court rejected an election petition filed by Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Vinayak Raut challenging the 2024 Lok Sabha election win of BJP MP Narayan Rane from the Ratnagiri-Sindhudurg constituency. [Vinayak Raut v. Election Commission of India & Ors] Justice Shailesh P Brahme allowed an interim application filed by Rane under Order VII Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure (CPC) seeking rejection of the election petition at the threshold. Justice Shailesh Brahme The Court held that Raut failed to disclose a valid cause of action due to non-compliance with Section 83(1) of the Representation of the People Act, 1951. Rane had secured 4,48,514 votes against Raut’s 4,00,656 votes in the election. In his petition, Raut alleged corrupt practices by BJP workers, including voter bribing and campaigning beyond the Model Code of Conduct deadline. However, Justice Brahme observed that the allegations contained in the petition lacked fundamental material details. “The corrupt practice as alleged is very vague and lacks material particulars namely; time, place and identity of the persons who were campaigning. The news reports are also not sufficient to precisely corroborate the claim of Raut,” the Court held. The Court held that electronic evidence like pen drives cannot substitute material pleadings in election petitions, especially when petitioners fail to provide transcriptions. It concluded that omission of even a single material fact would lead to an incomplete cause of action. This would entitle the returning candidate to seek dismissal of the election petition. Senior Advocate Satish Maneshinde , along with Advocates Saket Mone, Srushti Thorat and Yuvraj Dhole, briefed by Vidhii Partners, appeared for Rane. Advocates Asim Sarode, Shriya Aawale, Saken Mujawar, Tushar Sonule and Prabuddha Borgaonkar represented Raut. [Read order]

items.title: CM Vijay, ministers must provide proof to prove claim of coverup in Veeramani POCSO case: DMK to Madras High Court
items.summary: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay and ministers Aadhav Arjuna and CTR Nirmal Kumar should furnish proof to prove their allegation that the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) had tried to cover up the Veeramani POCSO case when it was in power, the party told the Madras High Court on Wednesday. GEM Granites founder R Veeramani is currently in custody in a case under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (POCSO Act) over alleged sexual abuse of a minor. In the petition before the High Court, the DMK said that Vijay, Arjuna and Nirmal Kumar made public statements accusing the DMK of concealing the matter. The leaders also claimed that material evidence exists to support their assertions, as per the party. Considering these claims, the party has moved the High Court seeking a direction to the Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing the case to act on a September 27 representation by DMK Treasurer and Member of Parliament TR Baalu for examination of these three leaders. The matter was listed before Justice V Lakshminarayanan on Wednesday. Senior Advocate J Ravindran , appearing for the DMK, submitted that if the three leaders possess evidence showing a cover-up, they should hand it over to the police. Justice V Lakshminarayanan The Court, however, observed that the recently-constituted SIT should be allowed to conduct its investigation in peace and adjourned the matter by four weeks. No direction was issued at this stage requiring Vijay or the two ministers to appear before the SIT. The DMK has formally sought a writ of mandamus directing the SIT to consider and take action on Baalu's representation within a time frame fixed by the High Court. The representation seeks an inquiry into the source of the information on which Vijay and other leaders' statements were based and whether they had access to any investigation-related material that was not legitimately available to them. According to the affidavit, if Vijay and the two ministers possess documents, electronic material, communications or other evidence concerning the case, the same should be immediately secured and examined by the investigating agency. The DMK has argued that if their statements were not supported by any material, it needs to be examined how they made the claim of coverup.

items.title: Karnataka High Court stays forgery case against cult.fit co-founder Rishabh Telang
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on September 28 stayed the investigation in criminal proceedings initiated against fitness platform Cult.fit's co-founder Rishabh Telang on allegations of cheating, forgery and criminal breach of trust, among others [Rishabh Telang v. State of Karnataka]. Justice Anant Ramanath Hegde granted the interim stay on investigation and will hear the matter on September 30. "Since the matter is heard on merits, further investigation is stayed till the next date of hearing." Justice Anant Ramanath Hegde The case stemmed from a complaint filed by Telang’s brother-in-law and Cult co-founder Deepak Poduval accusing him of forging documents connected to the transfer of the original Cult business and the subsequent closure of Cult Fitness Private Limited. Bellandur Police lodged an FIR against Telang on August 6. Poduval alleged that he and Telang incorporated Cult Fitness in November 2015 as its only two subscribers, with each holding a 50 per cent stake. According to the complaint, Telang subsequently excluded him from the management of the company and diverted its business, customers, goodwill and revenue to Cultfit Healthcare Private Limited, which was incorporated in August 2016. Poduval further alleged that his signatures were forged on financial statements and documents submitted to the Registrar of Companies to have Cult Fitness struck off in 2019. He claimed that he discovered the alleged irregularities only after examining the company’s records in May and June 2026. The FIR invoked provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita concerning criminal breach of trust, cheating, forgery, use of forged documents and criminal conspiracy, along with Section 66D of the Information Technology Act. Senior Advocate Sandesh Chouta , appearing for Telang, submitted the dispute is a commercial in nature and that criminal proceedings have been initiated to harass his client. items.title: Karnataka High Court forms 3-judge panel to assess feasibility of more HC benches
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Tuesday constituted a three-member committee to examine the feasibility of establishing circuit or permanent benches of High Court at Mangaluru, Udupi, Shivamogga, Chikkamagaluru, Kodagu-Madikeri, Hassan, Davanagere and Uttara Kannada. The committee was constituted by the Chief Justice through a notification dated September 29. The three-member panel comprises Justice Anu Sivaraman , Justice SG Pandit and Justice Mohammad Nawaz . Justice Anu Sivaraman, Justice S G Pandit and Justice Mohammad Nawaz The notification states that the committee has been constituted to verify the feasibility of establishing a High Court circuit bench/permanent bench in the identified regions. The committee has also been directed to consult all stakeholders before submitting its report to the High Court on the feasibility of establishing such benches. The notification, issued by Registrar General M Chandrashekar Reddy, states that the committee will function with immediate effect. The issue assumes significance since Karnataka currently has the principal seat at Bengaluru and benches at Dharwad and Kalaburagi. items.title: RTE quota in private schools: Supreme Court pulls up NCPCR for indifference, asks chairperson to appear
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday pulled up the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) over its approach towards implementing the 25 percent reservation for children from weaker sections and disadvantaged groups in private unaided schools under the Right to Education Act [Dinesh Biwaji Ashtikar v. State of Maharashtra] A Bench of Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe expressed dissatisfaction with the manner in which the child rights body had responded to the issue. “How can they act so indifferent? items.title: Karnataka High Court grants ₹2.77 crore to man paralysed after tree branch fell on him; calls for use of AI to identify hazards
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently directed civic authorities to pay ₹2.77 crore with 6% interest to a Bengaluru resident who suffered permanent paraplegia after a branch of a Gulmohar tree fell on him while he was walking on a public road [Chandan G v. State of Karnataka]. Justice Suraj Govindaraj held that the BBMP (now Greater Bengaluru Authority) owed a statutory and public duty in relation to the tree even though it stood within the premises of a private school. The Court also found that the civic body had actual notice of the danger at least from February 22, 2024, before the incident that occured on March 7, 2024., Justice Suraj Govindraj It also called upon the State government to establish a mechanism by which a public safety hazard, once reported or detected, is addressed despite the responsibility being divided among different departments, authorities, contractors, utilities or private owners. "The object is to ensure that once a danger is brought to the notice of the competent authority, or is otherwise reasonably identified, the information is recorded, assessed according to the degree of risk, entrusted to a named person or authority and followed through until the danger is made safe and the remedial work is independently verified," it said. The Court thus issued a slew of guidelines including use of cameras and artificial intelligence (AI) to detect public safety hazards, maintenance of digital records, time-bound response depending on the level of threat, recurrence monitoring, preventive maintenance, periodic inspection etc. The petitioner suffered a severe spinal injury after a branch of a Gulmohar tree from the premises of Good Shepherd Convent School fell on him while he was walking to work. He underwent spinal decompression, stabilisation surgery and prolonged rehabilitation. His disability was assessed at 85%, while the Court treated his functional disability as 100% for calculating loss of future earning capacity. The Court assessed total compensation at ₹2,82,29,695, including ₹24,44,271 towards medical expenses, ₹1,03,85,424 towards loss of future earning capacity, ₹27 lakh towards attendant and care charges, ₹1.17 crore towards future medical, physiotherapy, massage and rehabilitation expenses, and ₹5 lakh each towards pain and suffering and loss of amenities. items.title: Will affect election: Calcutta HC dismisses plea flagging age discrepancy in BJP candidate Hasirani Rath's affidavit
items.summary: The Calcutta High Court recently dismissed a plea by the West Bengal Congress seeking verification of an alleged discrepancy in the election affidavit of Bharatiya Janata Party's (BJP) Nandigram bye-election candidate Hasirani Rath [West Bengal Pradesh Congress Committee & Anr. v Election Committee of India & Ors] . items.title: Calcutta High Court grants interim bail to Congress candidate Milan Pradhan to contest Nandigram by-polls
items.summary: The Calcutta High Court on Tuesday granted interim bail to Congress leader Milan Pradhan to enable him to contest the upcoming Nandigram bypolls. Pradhan has been in custody in connection with six cases relating to the 2007 Nandigram violence. Justice Tirthankar Ghosh today ordered that Pradhan be released on interim bail till October 20 provided he furnishes a bond of ₹20,000 along with two sureties of ₹10,000 each. " I am of the opinion that petitioner may be granted an opportunity to contest the election and to that effect he may be released on interim bail," the Court said. The direction was part of separate orders passed on six bail pleas filed by Pradhan in connection with his arrest in six criminal cases from 2007, which involved allegations of rioting and murder. Justice Tirthankar Ghosh In his petitions, Pradhan questioned the timing of his arrest, given that the cases against him were from nearly two decades ago. This was one of the factors taken note of by the High Court while granting Pradhan interim bail. Another aspect factored in was the nature of the criminal cases in connection with which Pradhan was arrested. items.title: Ernst & Young moves Supreme Court over tax on employees seconded from US to India
items.summary: Ernst & Young US LLP (EY US) has moved the Supreme Court challenging a Delhi High Court judgment concerning the taxability of payments received in relation to employees seconded to EY entities in India. [EY Vs Union of India] The appeal challenges a June 18 judgment by a Division Bench of Justices V Kameswar Rao and Vinod Kumar , which ruled in favour of the Income Tax Department on the secondment issue. The judgment arose from five appeals concerning assessment years 2018-19 to 2022-23. The principal issue before the High Court was whether payments received by EY US in connection with seconded employees could be taxed as fees for technical services (FTS) under Article 12 of the India-US Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (DTAA). The Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) earlier ruled in favour of EY US and treated the payments as cost-to-cost reimbursements. It also held that the seconded personnel became employees of the Indian entities during the period of their secondment. The High Court disagreed with the ITAT. It noted that the employees were seconded to India for limited period of two to three years and returned to EY US once the assignment ended. The Court also found that the Indian entities could terminate the secondment but could not sever the employees' underlying relationship with EY US. The Bench further examined the nature of the work performed by the secondees and found that they were involved in training employees, implementing EY Group policies and processes and maintaining quality standards in the Indian entities. Therefore, the High Court held that the services satisfied the "make available" requirement under Article 12(4)(b) of the DTAA. Court said, “ The services rendered by the assessee herein includes technical services which would satisfy the ‘make available’ test, for the reason that there is a transfer of skill/knowledge. ” The High Court also rejected EY US' argument that there was no transfer of technical know-how or expertise, observing that the scope of services showed that the seconded employees imparted training. It added that EY US retained a lien over the seconded employees since they returned to the US entity after their Indian assignments. Consequently, the Court set aside the ITAT orders in all five appeals and answered the question concerning secondment payments in favour of the Revenue and against EY US. items.title: Delhi High Court slaps ₹1 lakh costs on advocate for attending hearing from moving car
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has imposed costs of ₹1 lakh on an advocate for appearing in a virtual hearing from a moving car. Justice Om Prakash Shukla observed that the convenience of virtual proceedings cannot come at the cost of courtroom decorum or cause disturbance in the conduct of judicial proceedings. "When this Court has to deal with more than 70 matters in a day, background noise and movement during the hearing are disruptive for this Court to proceed," the Bench said. Justice Om Prakash Shukla It added that even the High Court's Electronic Evidence and Video Conferencing Rules, 2025 state that an endeavour shall be made by advocates not to join proceedings from vehicles, except in exceptional circumstances and with the permission of the Court. "The requirement is not merely procedural and to ensure that even when Counsel appear virtually, they do so from an environment conducive to the proper functioning of this Court. There is no such exceptional circumstances existing in the present matter and the conduct of the Counsel is in violation of the rules," the Court said. Therefore, it ordered Advocate Nachiketa Goyal to deposit the ₹1 lakh fine with the Delhi High Court Legal Services Committee (DHCLSC). The High Court passed the order while hearing enforcement proceedings initiated by South Indian Bank and Union Bank of India against the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI). items.title: Kerala High Court quashes State decision to abolish Kerala Police Officers Association
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Tuesday quashed the State government's decision to dissolve the Kerala Police Officers Association (KPOA), as part of its move to restructure associations formed by police officers in Kerala [ Kerala Police Officers Association v State of Kerala & connected cases ]. The State Home Department's order was aimed at reorganising three associations representing different ranks of police personnel. The State's move resulted in the dissolution of one of the three police associations (KPOA), while the remaining two were to be retained in a reorganised form. This was challenged before the High Court by the KPOA. Justice Bechu Kurian Thomas today ruled in KPOA's favour, holding that the State did not have the power to restructure the three police associations in the way it did, that its decision interfered with the constitutional right of the police officers to continue in their associations. "The recognition granted to the members of the police force to form associations has not been revoked either by the State Police Chief or even by the government. Thus under no circumstances could the government have interfered with the structure of the recognized police associations ," it added. The Court further held that the freedom to form associations guaranteed under Article 19(1)(c) of the Constitution is not exhausted once an association is formed, but extends to preserving the association and its composition. " The freedom to form an association and freedom to continue the association are both facets of Article 19(1)(c) of the Constitution, " the Court said. Justice Bechu Kurian Thomas The ruling came on petitions challenging a government order dated July 27, 2026. The order had abolished the KPOA and reorganised the membership of the two remaining bodies - the Kerala Police Association (KPA) and Kerala Police Senior Officers Association (KPSOA). The government order had also directed that the KPOA's assets, including its bank accounts, documents, deposits, investments, rights and liabilities, were to be distributed between the two remaining bodies in a 60:40 ratio. It further stated that ad hoc committees would take over certain administrative duties and that elections to the newly constituted associations would be conducted by September 30. items.title: From 'just one more' to 'buy the whole damn pack': Allahabad High Court judge writes poem on dangers of smoking
items.summary: Justice Shekhar B Saraf of Allahabad High Court has written a poem to highlight the dangers of smoking. Justice Saraf annexed the poem to a judgment delivered by him and Justice Abdhesh Kumar Chaudhary on Tuesday on the illegality of serving hookah in the restaurants in Uttar Pradesh . "From my own experience of smoking, I pen these last paragraphs in an attempt to educate the young generation of this country to not become a prey to the deleterious and indelible habit of tobacco smoking," Justice Saraf said. The judge writes that he was an unwilling smoker in the beginning but it soon turned into a habit. "I entered law school pure as morning dew, Sneered at the smokers puffing by the gate, “Weak-willed,” I scoffed, “I’d never join that crew” Famous last words. Reader, I was bait. It started with a ‘chaii’, innocent and warm, A senior offered, “Try one, just for fun.” I took it like a soldier joins a storm Bravely, stupidly, and one by one. The “occasional” ‘sutta’ soon grew bold, It multiplied like rabbits, unrestrained." The judge went on to highlight how smoking became a norm for him. "My lungs, once mine, were quietly sold To a landlord who never once explained the lease. I told myself I merely dabbled, A social smoker, cultured, in control. items.title: 2021 Antilia bomb scare: Mumbai court grants bail to Sachin Waze, says no evidence Ambani family was terrorised
items.summary: A special National Investigation Agency (NIA) court in Mumbai has granted bail to former police officer Sachin Waze in the 2021 Antilia bomb scare and Mansukh Hiran murder case. NIA sought a stay on the order, however, the same was rejected by the special court. In the order of September 29, special judge Chakor S Baviskar questioned the applicability of terrorism charges under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA). The court found a significant flaw in the prosecution's case regarding the explosives-laden SUV parked near Mukesh Ambani's residence. It noted a complete absence of witness statements from the Ambani family. “The prosecution is not coming up with any specific case that, exactly in whose mind accused Sachin (Waze) wanted to create terror... The court observed that after the incident, the target and other family members are very much available generally and easily. “Office of the Investigating Agency i.e. of the NIA and the Antilia, i.e. residence of the Ambanis, are literally just wall to wall adjacent!” the judge said. It highlighted that key co-accused Pradeep Sharma and Sunil Mane had already secured bail. The parity principle heavily favored Waze, who has been incarcerated since his March 2021 arrest. items.title: Allahabad High Court protects CJP activist from arrest over video of government school
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court on September 28 granted interim protection from arrest to Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) member Gaurav Bharti in connection with an first information report (FIR) registered against him for filming the dilapidated condition of a government primary school in Farrukhabad [ Gaurav Bharti @ Gaurav Kumar v. State of U.P. and 3 Others] . A Division Bench comprising Justice Salil Kumar Rai and Padam Narain Mishra issued the direction on petition filed by Bharti seeking the quashing of the criminal proceedings initiated against him. "The petitioner shall not be arrested in pursuance of the First Information Report dated 19.08.2026, registered as Case Crime No. 0246 of 2026, under Sections 352 and 353 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 and Section 66 of the Information Technology Act, 2000, Police Station- Nawabganj, District Fatehgarh," the Court directed. The controversy stemmed from an FIR registered on August 19 at Nawabganj Police Station in Fatehgarh district. According to the FIR, the petitioner was accused of having "illegally prepared a video of the institution and had misrepresented the condition of the institution." Bharti recorded the footage as part of the CJP’s ongoing 'School Thik Karo' campaign, an initiative aimed at highlighting poor civic infrastructure and lacking basic facilities in state-run primary schools. Justice Salil Kumar Rai Bharti's counsel contended that the recitals in the FIR were completely baseless and false. It was further argued that in any event, the petitioner could not be prosecuted for the offences in light of an earlier ruling of the High Court delivered this month. The Bench observed that "the matter requires consideration." It noted that the Additional Government Advocate had accepted notice on behalf of the State authorities and directed the issuance of notice to the complainant. items.title: Ten years on, still struggling to execute foreign arbitral award: Daiichi tells Supreme Court
items.summary: Japanese pharmaceutical company Daiichi Sankyo told the Supreme Court on Tuesday that nearly ten years after securing a foreign arbitral award against former Ranbaxy promoters Malvinder Mohan Singh and Shivinder Mohan Singh, it was still struggling to execute the award [Yes Bank Vs Daiichi Sankyo]. Senior Advocate Arvind Datar , appearing for Daiichi, said the company had pursued arbitration, obtained an award on April 29, 2016 and then initiated execution proceedings, but was yet to realise the award. " It’s 10 years to execute an award, international award ,” Datar said. He added that the situation has become a “spider’s web”, with disputes continuing over what happened to shares of Fortis Healthcare Limited (FHL) held by the judgment debtors. Supreme Court, Arvind Datar The submissions were made before a Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana during the hearing of challenges by banks and financial institutions to the Delhi High Court’s directions for a forensic audit in the execution proceedings initiated by Daiichi. Datar told the Court that the banks and the judgment debtors have taken conflicting stands on whether certain Fortis shares were encumbered, who invoked the pledges and who ultimately sold the shares. “The banks blame the judgment-debtors, judgment-debtors blame the bank, and I am the decree-holder, I am not getting any relief at all, ” he submitted. Datar also explained why Daiichi had earlier stated that it did not want to pursue a forensic audit against the banks. He said there were 17 banks involved and that Daiichi had taken the stand out of “sheer frustration”, since hearing every bank separately would further prolong the execution proceedings. items.title: Rajah & Tann's Ng Kim Beng on the firm's growth story, AI and PE-backed law firms
items.summary: Ng Kim Beng took over as Managing Partner of Rajah & Tann, Singapore a year back. In this conversation with Bar & Bench's Pallavi Saluja, Beng talks about why the firm has grown from just over 30 lawyers to more than 1,100, why India remains part of the firm's vision and why AI's efficiency gains haven't touched the billable hour just yet. He is candid, too, about what worries him: a wave of US firms turning to private equity funding that Asian firms, without similar backing, may struggle to match. [Watch Interview] Edited excerpts follow. Pallavi Saluja (PS): What have been your priorities since you took over as Managing Partner at Rajah & Tann a year ago? Ng Kim Beng (NKB): My predecessor Patrick Ang laid out: people, processes and practice. On people - making sure we continue to attract and retain the right talent and support their growth. One topic that's very current within the firm is the profession's sustainability and, within that, career prospects for younger lawyers. They're often unfairly labelled as a "softer generation," but I think they come with ambition, drive and motivation, on top of the evergreen qualities of diligence and industry. What's changed is a sense of purpose. In my time, that came easily: you joined a good firm, worked under a good mentor, kept your head down and a path more or less opened up for you. That's changed now. The space is far more crowded, competition among peers is sharper, clients are more sophisticated and technology has accelerated all of it. It's about helping them navigate those conditions and helping them see a future for themselves here. On process, the firm has grown enormously since I joined straight out of university, when we had just over 30 lawyers. Today we're 450 fee earners in Singapore and over 1,100 across Southeast Asia. Some of our systems and processes have served us well but are now worn and need upgrading and replacement. We need clearer, more consistent processes and better centralised support, making sure that it is set up in a way that there is a good degree of accessibility. One thing I've learned is that management can end up in a bubble: colleagues out doing hearings and travelling for work don't always know what support is available at HQ. So communicating that accessibility matters just as much as building the systems themselves. Finally, practice is probably the most important of the three, because it's what funds everything else. items.summary: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. A Raja, the district armed reserve constable, who was seen firing from atop a police vehicle during the 2018 anti-Sterlite protests in Thoothukudi, died on Tuesday, September 29, after undergoing treatment for health complications. According to reports, Raja had served in the Tamil Nadu police for more than two decades. He joined the police force in 2003 and was serving in the Thoothukudi district armed reserve. He was recently transferred to the law and order wing at the Kulasekarapattinam police station. However, he had not joined his new posting, as he was undergoing treatment for kidney and liver-related ailments. Raja is survived by his wife and two sons, who are pursuing college education. Raja came to public attention after photographs and videos of the police firing during the anti-Sterlite protests in May 2018 were widely circulated. One of the photographs showed a policeman wearing a yellow and black T-shirt, standing atop a police vehicle and firing at the protestors. The policeman was later identified as Raja. The protests against Sterlite Copper had continued for nearly 100 days, with residents demanding the plant be shut down, citing environmental and health concerns. The situation escalated, and the police opened fire on the protesters. Eleven people were killed on May 22. The firing continued on May 23, when 22-year-old Kaliyappan was killed. Another person who sustained injuries in the firing died in October 2018 while undergoing treatment. In all, 13 people died in connection with the firing, including 17-year-old Snowlin Jackson. More than 100 people were injured during the two days of police firing. A Commission, headed by retired judge Aruna Jagadeesan, was constituted to inquire into the circumstances surrounding the firing. It examined photographs and other evidence from the incident and recommended action against seventeen police personnel, including Raja and other officials, including the district collector and three Deputy Tahsildars. items.title: Karnataka’s new data centre policy puts water, energy in focus: What does it say?
items.summary: Karnataka wants to dramatically expand its data centre footprint. But this time, the state says the growth must come with a tighter check on how much power and water these facilities consume. Its new Sustainable Data Centre Policy 2026–2031 targets 1 GW of cumulative data centre IT load by 2031 and a 10–12% share of India’s AI-ready data centre ecosystem. At the same time, it proposes incentives linked to energy and water efficiency, resource mapping to identify areas with adequate power and water, and greater use of renewable energy and treated water. The shift comes as Karnataka already has 32 data centres, even as questions remain over how much water the existing facilities consume. TNM had earlier reported that neither the Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board (BWSSB) nor the Karnataka State Pollution Control Board (KSPCB) separately tracked water use by data centres. The IT department estimated that the state's 32 data centres consume around 4,000 kilolitres of water a day, based on informal inputs from operators. Now, the new policy proposes to map water and energy availability across existing and proposed data centre locations before planning further expansion. Renewable energy, energy efficiency and water conservation The policy encourages data centres to increase their use of renewable energy through state power procurement and open-access mechanisms. It also introduces incentives linked directly to how efficiently data centres use electricity and water. Data centres will have to report Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) and Water Usage Effectiveness (WUE) on a plant-wise basis. PUE measures the total energy consumed by a facility against the energy used by its IT equipment, while WUE measures water consumption in relation to IT energy consumption. PUE is calculated by dividing a data centre’s total energy consumption by the energy used by its IT equipment. A PUE of 1.0 is ideal, as it means all the power is being used by the computing equipment, with no additional consumption for cooling and other supporting systems. WUE measures how much water a data centre uses for every unit of energy consumed by its IT equipment. It is calculated by dividing annual water consumption in litres by IT equipment energy consumption in kWh. A lower WUE indicates lower water use. items.title: EAM Jaishankar warns of food crisis, Opposition targets Modi govt on readiness
items.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar has warned that a major global food crisis could hit in the coming months, driven by severe fertiliser shortages, blocked grain shipments, and ongoing wars. Speaking at an Asia Society event in New York, Jaishankar said expanding conflicts in eastern Europe and West Asia are squeezing trade routes and hitting developing nations the hardest. Jaishankar pointed out that key grain exporters are struggling to ship supplies through the Black Sea, while major fertiliser producers in Russia and West Asia face heavy production and transit disruptions. Combined with tight energy markets, capital flight, and extreme weather patterns like El Niño, he said the global economy is facing a combined squeeze on food, fuel, fertiliser, and finance. He also criticised richer nations for taking self-centred policy decisions that ignore the basic needs of vulnerable countries. The Minister’s statements quickly triggered sharp reactions from domestic opposition parties, who accused the Union government of using global problems to cover up internal mismanagement. Led by the Congress, opposition leaders questioned whether India has enough safeguards in place to protect its own farmers and consumers from the fallout. Opposition members demanded clear data from the Union Agriculture Ministry on national stocks of essential fertilisers, particularly Urea and Di-ammonium Phosphate (DAP), ahead of the upcoming sowing season. They argued that while the Centre speaks about global risks on foreign platforms, local farmers are already dealing with high input costs and irregular supply. Critics also questioned the government's trade policies, warning that allowing grain exports while predicting a global shortfall could push up food prices at home. They called for direct subsidies and immediate relief measures to protect small farmers from rising costs and bad weather. Government officials pushed back against the criticism, stating that India's domestic buffer stocks for major foodgrains like rice and wheat remain comfortably above required safety limits. Official sources added that long-term import deals are already in place to keep fertiliser supplies steady. However, with global trade routes facing continued stress, the debate over India's farm security and supply management is set to intensify.

items.title: Kerala govt orders vigilance probe into Kochi Life-Mission flat construction defects
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. The Kerala government has ordered a Vigilance probe into the construction defects, structural compromises, and financial irregularities surrounding the P and T Apartment complex at Mundamveli in Ernakulam. The housing complex, home to 78 families, was built under the LIFE Mission housing scheme and implemented by the Greater Cochin Development Authority (GCDA) to rehabilitate the families who lived in the waterlogging-prone P and Colony. The government order followed an inspection report submitted by the Director of the Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (VACB). According to the order, the government has sanctioned a preliminary probe under Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act. Speaking to the media, the apartment’s residents’ association president said the residents welcome the vigilance inquiry. The government order for the vigilance inquiry came days after the Chief Minister VD Satheesan declared that the housing complex would be demolished and residents rehabilitated. According to the residents , within a month of moving in, major leaks surfaced in many houses following the rain. Later, multiple issues began to appear, including cracks on walls and plaster breaking apart like powder. Many residents also complained about electric shocks, especially during the rainy season. Abhilash said neither the GCDA nor the Kochi Corporation showed any willingness to address their issues. Following repeated negligence from authorities, the residents began an indefinite strike in front of the apartment two months ago. On the 67th day of their protest, September 26, VD Satheesan made a declaration of demolition and rehabilitation. Satheesan also added that detailed decisions regarding the same will be announced later. Though the families expressed happiness in the CM’s comments, they said they will not stop the protest until a definite solution is etched out.

items.title: Kavin caste murder: HC quashes chargesheet against parents, finds no proof they met accused
